payload.reason: The evidence provides a clear definition and explanation of second-order co-occurrence matrices, detailing their construction and application in measuring semantic relatedness.

claims.text: A second-order co-occurrence matrix is constructed by averaging first-order co-occurrence vectors associated with terms, which represent the meaning of the terms.
Second-order co-occurrence vectors incorporate contextual information and semantic similarity scores derived from taxonomies to measure relatedness between concepts.
Integrating semantic similarity into second-order co-occurrence vectors improves correlation with human judgments for similarity and relatedness.
